chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Zakariyya ibn Adam, from al-Kahili, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The 'Aqiqa is on the seventh day, and the midwife is given the shank and the thigh, and the bone is not broken."

key_terms.الرَّجْلَ: The shank: the lower part of the leg, a specific cut of meat
key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةُ: Aqiqa: the sacrificial animal offered for a newborn child
key_terms.الْقَابِلَةُ: The midwife: the woman who assists in childbirth
key_terms.الْوَرِكَ: The thigh: the upper part of the leg, a specific cut of meat
key_terms.لَا يُكْسَرُ الْعَظْمُ: The bone is not broken: a recommended practice during slaughter
key_terms.يَوْمَ السَّابِعِ: On the seventh day: the prescribed time for the sacrifice

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rulings for the 'Aqiqa sacrifice regarding timing and the midwife's share?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the Sunnah of the 'Aqiqa on the seventh day, linking it to the naming and circumcising rituals. It specifically prescribes giving the shank (qabla) and thigh (warik) to the midwife, reflecting the customary honor given to her, while emphasizing the preservation of the bones to ensure the meat is served respectfully.
